chapter: Brass band and the Lyric Theater
title: Carrying drums, streetcar permits and Excelsior Brass Band
summary: He doesn't regret ignoring his father's advice; recalls getting streetcar permits for drums and playing parades and funerals with the Excelsior Brass Band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: By the way, do you regret your father's advice not taking it, you know? I mean...

Well, no. I liked it what I liked and that was it. You don't mind carrying all those drums? I don't mind carrying it. And we have it easy now because we have a lot of transportation. Definitely before. Before you had to get on the street car and you had to go to public service and get a permit. And if you wouldn't have that permit, the conductor wouldn't leave you on. Did you charge the same fare as the regular? Same regular fare, but didn't charge you no fare for your drums. Yeah. Did you ever play any parades that you had to carry your drums in the marching parades? Oh, yeah. I played the Excelsior Brass Band. Excelsior? Yeah. When was that? About how long ago? About 30 years ago. 25, 30 years ago.
That was after World War I, huh?

I think it was before Depression. Because lots of times I played funeral with them and played parade. Then when they had dance at the background, I used to play with them in the brass band at the background. And Kid Rene was upstairs in a dance hall. She used to have two bands. Kid Rene would be upstairs and the brass band would be downstairs.
